articles.title: Ghost in the Cell review – Indonesian prison-slasher-satire contains the most unhinged punch-up in decades
articles.summary: Director Joko Anwar uses horror for social commentary as he skewers corruption and hypocrisy with likable silliness and raucous energy. Given the 2020s horror boom, Indonesia’s prolific Joko Anwar – who has worked more often in that genre than any other – should be better known.
body: Fitted up for the murder of his boss, who is found gutted and spreadeagled on a ceiling fan, timid investigative journalist Dimas (Endy Arfian) winds up in the slammer. But murder, immediately followed by the flamboyant flaying of the victim, dogs him wherever he goes: the prison hitman assigned to dispose of him is in turn found in the washroom rendered into flesh origami. Charismatic prison refusenik Anggoro (Abimana Aryasatya) takes Dimas under his wing; as the victims stack up, an apparently clairvoyant member of his clique called Six (Yoga Pratama) admits that all of them manifested a red aura, signifying anger, prior to dying.

You suspect Anwar himself is no stranger to the old red aura from time to time: from the warden-facilitated drug-dealing network to the separate wing of pampered elitist offenders, his film overspills with droll outrage over Indonesian corruption. Dimas’s exposé of an illegal forestry scheme is what appears to have dislodged the demonic entity that is now attached to him, and feeding off the local abundance of negative energy. But Six figures out that partaking in wholesome activities, like praying and dancing, lowers their chances of being picked off.
points: Director Joko Anwar uses horror for social commentary as he skewers corruption and hypocrisy with likable silliness and raucous energy.
Given the 2020s horror boom, Indonesia’s prolific Joko Anwar – who has worked more often in that genre than any other – should be better known.

articles.title: After the Snowmelt review – a fatal disaster in a snowstorm leads to devastating act of remembrance
articles.summary: Yi-Shan Lo returns to Nepal to follow the route of her best friend’s ill-fated hike in a harrowing but cathartic documentary. A work of deep personal reckoning, Yi-Shan Lo’s debut documentary feature opens with closeups of the film-maker’s own footsteps as she trudges through a snowbound landscape.
body: Struggling to make sense of these events, Lo painstakingly retraces the days leading up to and during her friends’ disappearance. She pores over old text messages, Chun’s diaries and footage captured by the Nepali rescue team. These materials shed some light on the ordeal, as well as the pair’s backgrounds. Diving into her personal archive, Lo recalls her burgeoning friendship with Chun at their Catholic girls’ school, where the latter defiantly resisted the institution’s rigid dress codes. Considering Chun’s efforts to express his non-conforming identity and his use of male pronouns, it is even more devastating that he was repeatedly misgendered in death by various news reports.

Revelatory as they might be, these artefacts appear insubstantial next to the weight of grief. In the second half of the film, Lo physically returns to the trail of the fateful trek. As digital screens and paper scraps give way to the vistas of babbling brooks and verdant hills, film-making emerges as a cathartic gesture of remembrance. Through Lo’s lens, the cave where Chun and Yueh took shelter ceases only to be a site of trauma, but a shrine to the memories of their love.
points: Yi-Shan Lo returns to Nepal to follow the route of her best friend’s ill-fated hike in a harrowing but cathartic documentary.

articles.title: Selena Gomez Reveals Vaping Nicotine Changed Her Voice: ‘It’s Not Worth It’
articles.summary: Selena Gomez said heavy nicotine vaping has changed her voice, and told fans she has now quit the habit. The singer, actor and Rare Beauty founder, 34, spoke about it in a video of roughly a minute posted to her Instagram Story on Sunday. “I’m not going to be able to change my voice,” Gomez
body: She said she was excited to have stopped and hoped she could keep it up, though it was hard.
“But I know if you are going through something, you can get through it too,” she said. “It sucks.”
Gomez did not cite vaping when she answered repeated fan questions about her voice during an Instagram Live session last December. At the time, she said her throat sometimes swells on the inside.

Gomez has been open about her health over the years. She has lupus and received a kidney transplant in 2017, and she has spoken publicly about her bipolar disorder diagnosis, including in the 2022 documentary “Selena Gomez: My Mind & Me.”

articles.title: Seventeen’s Jeonghan and Joshua Find Their JxJ Duo Sound on ‘Dreamscape’: ‘Right in the Middle Between Strong and Subtle’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: For more than a decade, Seventeen’s Jeonghan and Joshua have shared the spotlight with 11 bandmates in one of K-pop’s best-selling groups. Now they get it to themselves with “Dreamscape,” their first album as the duo JxJ.
body: Joshua says their company first suggested they collaborate together. “After giving it some thought, we’ve been together for so long, and we really wanted to show a different side to ourselves,” he says. “Sides that we haven’t shown as a whole group, as Seventeen, so we thought it was going to be fun. And a lot of our fans actually like our chemistry, the chemistry that the two of us have.”

Jeonghan says that with several members away on military service, those who remained talked with the company about how to keep bringing Carats new music. “We thought that it would be a really exciting project, so that’s how it came to life.”

articles.title: ‘A beautiful dismantling of cynicism’: why Galaxy Quest is my feelgood movie
articles.summary: The latest in our series of writers detailing their most easily rewatched comfort films is an appreciation of a smart, funny and tender ode to fan culture. “By Grabthar’s hammer, by the sons of Worvan … you shall be avenged.” If you have seen Galaxy Quest, those words may bring you close to tears.
body: 1999’s Galaxy Quest is such a good sci-fi parody that it was once voted the seventh best Star Trek film of all time … by Star Trek fans. Its genre send-up is effective and affectionate, with gags about underwritten female characters and illogical spaceship design. It is also a genuinely fun space caper: there’s a properly scary baddie, a spaceship chase sequence, a high-jeopardy mission on a foreign planet and not one but two romantic subplots. There are Beryllium spheres and a rock monster and an Omega-13 (whatever that is).

Rickman’s character, Alexander Dane, is one of a group of washed-up actors from a cancelled cult 1980s sci-fi show, now reduced to appearing at fan conventions. He’s joined by Sigourney Weaver’s continually objectified Gwen DeMarco (“My TV Guide interview was six paragraphs about my boobs and how they fit into my suit”), Tony Shalhoub’s eternally laid-back (read: stoned) Fred Kwan, Daryl Mitchell as former child star Tommy Webber and the show’s insufferable lead, Tim Allen’s Jason Nesmith, AKA “Commander Peter Quincy Taggart”.

articles.title: Rajinikanth’s ‘Jailer 2’ Ranks No. 2 at Global Box Office as ‘Street Fighter’ Leads
articles.summary: Indian superstar Rajinikanth’s Tamil-language action comedy “Jailer 2” was the second-biggest film in the world over the Oct. 16–18 weekend, grossing $31.2 million, according to Rentrak estimates. Only Paramount’s “Street Fighter,” with $51.1 million, earned more.
body: Tamil Nadu, the southern Indian state where the Tamil-language film industry is based, delivered the biggest share at $8.4 million. The neighboring southern Indian states of Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana supplied most of the remainder.

In North America, where the film is distributed by Shloka Entertainments, “Jailer 2” grossed $3.2 million over the Friday-to-Sunday frame, debuting at No. 9, taking its total to $5.2 million. Shloka said the film crossed $2 million on its opening day in the territory.

“Jailer 2” follows the 2023 hit “Jailer,” in which Rajinikanth played a retired prison warden drawn back into violence when an idol smuggler threatens his family. He returns as “Tiger” Muthuvel Pandian, with Ramya Krishnan, Yogi Babu and Mirnaa also reprising their roles. New to the franchise are Tamil actor S.J. Suryah as Bodhi Kalpak and Bollywood star Vidya Balan as Kaantha. Veteran Bollywood actor Mithun Chakraborty and Malayalam cinema actor Suraj Venjaramoodu also join the cast. Dilipkumar wrote and directed both films for Kalanithi Maran’s Sun Pictures, and Anirudh Ravichander again composed the music.

articles.title: Selena Gomez says vaping has affected her voice
articles.summary: The 34-year-old says vaping nicotine "a lot" permanently affected her singing and speaking voice.
body: Selena Gomez has said vaping nicotine has changed the way her voice sounds.
"I'm not gonna be able to change my voice," the singer, 34, said in a candid Instagram post, external on Sunday. "I vaped nicotine a lot."
"Nicotine is so hard to quit and I just wanted to say, if you're going through it, or if you're even trying to vape, it's just not worth it," she continued.
"It's so stupid and it changed my voice," she reiterated, then laughed: "So if you guys don't like listening to my voice, that's totally understandable. I don't mind. Just don't listen to it."

articles.title: Elizabeth Holmes documentary You Can See Everything debuts with huge $15m opening weekend
articles.summary: Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s buzzy film was shown on only 855 screens in the biggest documentary opening in North America since Fahrenheit 9/11 in 2004. Nathan Fielder’s nearly three-hour Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything, has opened to an extraordinary $15m domestic box…
body: You Can See Everything, directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, made $15m (A$21.5m, £11.2m) from only 855 screens, and had more than 2,000 sold-out screenings at the weekend, according to the production company A24. It is the biggest opening for a film playing on fewer than 1,000 screens since Borat opened to $26.5m in 2006.

It is also the biggest opening for a documentary in North America in two decades, since Fahrenheit 9/11 made nearly $24m from 868 theaters. Those numbers do not account for inflation or for concert films: Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour holds the record with a $92.8m opening weekend in 2023 when it was released in nearly 4,000 cinemas.
You Can See Everything has not opened at the international box office yet, coming out in Australia on 12 November and in the UK on 20 November.

Like other hits this year, including Backrooms and Obsession, ticket sales for You Can See Everything were driven by a largely younger audience in North America; more than 70% of the opening weekend crowd were under 35.

articles.title: Apu is Back! Veteran Voice Actor Sunil Malhotra Revives ‘The Simpsons’ Character After Nearly 10 Years
articles.summary: The 'The Legend of Korra' and 'The Legend of Vox Machina' actor takes over the role from Hank Azaria, who dropped the character following the release of the 2017 documentary 'The Problem With Apu.'
body: After almost a decade away, Apu Nahasapeemapetilon will be making a return to The Simpsons. The beloved bullet-magnet Kwik-E-Mart owner, one of the show’s most iconic characters from the golden age of the long-running Fox animated comedy series, is set to be a Springfield regular again as producers cast veteran voice actor Sunil Malhotra in the role.
Apu made his comeback in the season 38 episode, “Treehouse of Horror Presents: The Revengening” that aired on Sunday.

Malhotra takes over the role from Hank Azaria, the legendary Simpsons voice actor who voices many of the show’s characters including Moe Szyslak, Chief Wiggum, Comic Book Guy, Professor Frink, Dr. Nick Riviera and Snake Jailbird. Azaria famously decided to stop voicing Apu following controversy over the character in the 2010s, with a growing number of people pointing to the character reinforcing racial stereotypes about South Asians and the problematic nature of a white man voicing Apu.

articles.title: ‘My Notes on Mars,’ ‘Moonglow’ and ‘The Secret Lives of Baba Segi’s Wives’: LFF Tea With Filmmakers
articles.summary: THR caught up with some writers and directors during BFI London Film Festival-organized meet-ups.
body: The 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival (LFF) may have come to an end, with its winners unveiled on Sunday. But some of the filmmakers in attendance found themselves discussing their featured movies at fest-organized events with members of the press over the course of the celebration of cinema.
THR swung by a Filmmaker Afternoon Tea session to catch up with some of the creatives at LFF 2026 and hear from them.

Isabel Sandoval discusses Moonglow The LFF knew how to get people interested in Sandoval’s new movie, written and directed by the filmmaker who also stars in it. “The queen of sensual cinema returns with a 1970s Manila-set neo-noir about a police officer-turned-criminal under investigation by her former lover,” its website noted. “It’s not a whodunnit, but a why did she do it,” the filmmaker ( Lingua Franca ) told THR. “And it’s a subversion of a few elements of noir. The female character is not just your femme fatale. She’s actually a morally complicated, ethically compromised character.”
